flawed_step: Step 4: a colour-respecting bijection between ordered pairs need not have the product form (u,v) ↦ (f(u),f(v)); equal stable colour multisets do not supply a coherent vertex bijection.
counterexample: The 4×4 rook graph and the Cayley graph on Z_4^2 with connection set {±(1,0), ±(0,1), ±(1,1)} are non-isomorphic but are not distinguished by 2-WL.
assessment_summary:
Attempted proof and full audit:

1. Suppose graphs G and H have equal stable 2-WL colour multisets; to prove the statement, it would suffice to deduce G ≅ H. Judgment: JUSTIFIED — this is the contrapositive formulation of the desired claim.

2. Equality of the stable multisets implies |V(G)|²=|V(H)|², hence |V(G)|=|V(H)|. Judgment: JUSTIFIED — each multiset contains one colour for every ordered vertex pair.

3. Because the colour multiplicities agree, one can match the ordered pairs of G and H colour by colour, obtaining a colour-preserving bijection F:V(G)²→V(H)². Judgment: JUSTIFIED — equal finite multisets permit such a matching.

4. Claim that F can be chosen as F(u,v)=(f(u),f(v)) for a single bijection f:V(G)→V(H). Judgment: NOT JUSTIFIED — multiset equality gives an arbitrary matching of pairs and contains no requirement that matched pairs share coordinates coherently. This is the first failure.

5. If such an f existed, it would preserve equality and adjacency because every refined colour retains its preceding colour and therefore its initial colour (u=v, uv∈E); consequently f would be an isomorphism. Judgment: CONDITIONALLY JUSTIFIED — the implication is correct, but Step 4 did not establish the required f.

6. Therefore equal stable colour multisets imply G≅H, so all non-isomorphic graphs are distinguished. Judgment: NOT JUSTIFIED — the conclusion depends on the failed Step 4.

The failure is substantive, as the following verification shows.

7. Let R have vertex set Z_4², with distinct (i,j),(i',j') adjacent exactly when i=i' or j=j'. Let S be the Cayley graph on Z_4² with connection set C={±a,±b,±c}, where a=(1,0), b=(0,1), and c=(1,1). Judgment: JUSTIFIED — these definitions produce finite simple undirected graphs.

8. R has 16 vertices, degree 6, two common neighbours for adjacent vertices, and two common neighbours for nonadjacent vertices. Judgment: JUSTIFIED — an adjacent pair has the other two vertices in its shared row or column; a nonadjacent pair has the two opposite corners of its rectangle.

9. S also has 16 vertices, degree 6, and every two distinct vertices have exactly two common neighbours. Judgment: JUSTIFIED — every nonzero d∈Z_4² occurs exactly twice among ordered differences p−q with p,q∈C. For the order-two differences this follows from {a,−a}, {b,−b}, and {c,−c}; the other sign-classes are represented twice by {a,b}/{−a,−b}, {a,−b}/{−a,b}, {a,c}/{−a,−c}, {a,−c}/{−a,c}, {b,c}/{−b,−c}, and {b,−c}/{−b,c}. Common neighbours of x and y correspond to representations y−x=p−q.

10. In any graph with parameters (n,k,λ,μ), the first 2-WL refinement of a pair depends only on whether it is diagonal, an edge, or a nonedge. Judgment: JUSTIFIED — for a diagonal pair the multiplicities are 1 of (D,D), k of (E,E), and n−1−k of (N,N); for an edge they are 1 each of (D,E),(E,D), λ of (E,E), k−1−λ each of (E,N),(N,E), and n−2k+λ of (N,N); for a nonedge they are 1 each of (D,N),(N,D), μ of (E,E), k−μ each of (E,N),(N,E), and n−2−2k+μ of (N,N).

11. Since R and S both have parameters (16,6,2,2), induction over refinement rounds shows that corresponding diagonal, edge, and nonedge pairs receive the same shared colours in both graphs. Their stable colour multisets are therefore equal: 16 diagonal pairs, 96 ordered edges, and 144 ordered nonedges. Judgment: JUSTIFIED — Step 10 applies at every round because the new colour retains the old relation-class colour and the relevant multiplicities remain identical.

12. R and S are not isomorphic. Judgment: JUSTIFIED — R has a 4-clique consisting of any row. In S, translating any hypothetical 4-clique would make it contain 0, so its other three vertices would form a triangle in the subgraph induced by C; direct subtraction shows that this induced subgraph is the chordless 6-cycle a–c–b–(−a)–(−c)–(−b)–a, which has no triangle.

13. Thus R and S are non-isomorphic but have equal stable 2-WL colour multisets, so 2-WL does not distinguish every pair of non-isomorphic finite graphs. Judgment: JUSTIFIED — this follows from Steps 11 and 12 and refutes the statement.
